records.title: Graduation rate within 150% of normal time
records.excerpt: The share of an adjusted full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort completing within 150% of the program's normal time.
records.body: The IPEDS Graduation Rates component follows a defined entering cohort. The rate uses completers by 150% of normal time in the numerator and the original cohort less allowable exclusions in the denominator. It is not first-year retention and it is not the institution-wide percentage of all students who graduate.
records.calculation: completed within 150% of normal time / adjusted GR cohort
records.numerator: Adjusted-cohort members completing within 150% of normal time
records.denominator: Full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort less allowable exclusions
records.use: Use the governed GR cohort mart. Do not substitute a current enrollment population or the retention cohort.

records.title: Graduation rate within 200% of normal time
records.excerpt: The share of the adjusted GR cohort completing within twice the program's normal time.
records.body: GR200 uses the same governed cohort and allowable exclusion logic as the applicable Graduation Rates component, but extends the completion window to 200% of normal time. A bachelor's program with four years of normal time therefore uses an eight-year window.
records.calculation: completed within 200% of normal time / adjusted GR cohort
records.numerator: Adjusted-cohort members completing within 200% of normal time
records.use: Use for GR200 reporting; do not combine a different cohort with the longer completion window.

records.title: IPEDS Outcome Measures
records.excerpt: Completion and enrollment outcomes for four degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts defined by entering and attendance status.
records.body: The IPEDS Outcome Measures component follows first-time and non-first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, each split into full-time and part-time cohorts. It reports award and enrollment outcomes at specified follow-up points and covers a broader population than the full-time, first-time GR cohort.
records.use: Local award and enrollment outcomes are supported. Subsequent enrollment at another institution requires Clearinghouse or an equivalent external source and must remain flagged when unavailable.

records.title: Undergraduate admission rate
records.excerpt: Admitted first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants divided by applicants in the applicable admissions population.
records.body: The IPEDS Admissions component covers the selection process for entering first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at institutions without an open-admissions policy. Admission rate is sometimes called acceptance or selectivity rate, but the numerator and denominator must use the same governed applicant population and reporting term.
records.numerator: Applicants admitted in the governed ADM population
records.denominator: Applicants in the governed ADM population
records.use: Definition is governed, but the current applicant funnel is estimated from enrolled headcount. A production admissions-system extract is required before this rate is submission-ready.

records.title: Admissions yield
records.excerpt: Enrolled admitted students divided by admitted students for the same governed entering population.
records.body: Admissions yield describes how many admitted students subsequently enroll. It is distinct from admission rate: the denominator is admitted students, not all applicants.
records.denominator: Admitted students in the same governed ADM population
records.use: A production applicant and decision extract is required. Do not certify the current estimated applicant funnel.

records.title: Cost of attendance (COA)
records.excerpt: The applicable student budget combining tuition and fees with books, supplies, living costs, and other expenses.
records.body: For IPEDS Cost reporting, COA for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates includes tuition and required fees, books and supplies, food and housing, and other expenses. The applicable amount depends on residency and living arrangement. COA is a published budget, not the amount every student actually pays.
records.calculation: tuition and required fees + books and supplies + food and housing + other expenses
records.use: Use the governed cost schedule for the requested residency and living arrangement. Do not label COA as net price.

records.title: Tuition and required fees
records.excerpt: Published tuition plus fees required of the applicable student population.
records.body: Tuition and required fees are one component of cost of attendance. Optional charges and costs that vary solely by individual choice are not automatically included. The applicable level, residency, enrollment load, and academic period must be stated.
records.use: Use the published governed charge schedule; do not substitute total cost of attendance.

records.title: Average institutional net price
records.excerpt: Average cost of attendance minus average applicable grant and scholarship aid for the defined student cohort.
records.body: IPEDS average net price is calculated for specified full-time, first-time undergraduate aid cohorts. It moves beyond sticker price by subtracting grant and scholarship aid from cost of attendance; loans are not subtracted as grant aid.
records.source: NCES Average Institutional Net Price FAQ
records.calculation: average cost of attendance - average grant and scholarship aid
records.denominator: Applicable full-time, first-time undergraduate aid cohort
records.use: State the cohort and income band when applicable. Do not call tuition alone net price.

records.title: Total revenue
records.excerpt: Revenue recognized under the accounting standard and reporting scope applicable to the institution.
records.body: IPEDS Finance collects revenues by source under different formats for GASB and FASB reporters. Total revenue must reconcile to the applicable audited financial statements and cannot be reconstructed safely from a few operating categories.
records.use: The current finance mart is a limited planning summary, not an audited general-ledger contract. Obtain the audited GASB-aligned source before certification.

records.title: Total expenses
records.excerpt: Expenses recognized and classified under the institution's applicable accounting and IPEDS reporting standards.
records.body: IPEDS Finance collects expenses by function, such as instruction, research, academic support, and institutional support. A complete total must reconcile to audited financial statements and the correct GASB or FASB reporting form.
records.use: Do not certify the limited current finance mart as the institution's audited total expenses.

records.title: Net position
records.excerpt: For the public GASB reporting model, assets and deferred outflows less liabilities and deferred inflows.
records.body: Net position is a financial-statement measure, not cash on hand or annual operating surplus. IPEDS Finance classification must follow the institution's audited GASB statements and current survey instructions.
records.calculation: assets + deferred outflows - liabilities - deferred inflows
records.use: Require audited financial-statement mapping before using this value in a submission.

records.title: Instructional staff (instructional faculty)
records.excerpt: The IPEDS occupational category for employees whose primary occupation includes instruction.
records.body: IPEDS instructional staff includes employees classified as primarily instruction or instruction combined with research and/or public service. It is not interchangeable with every employee holding a faculty title, and it is independent of academic rank or tenure status.
records.use: Classify from the governed HR occupational assignment; do not infer from department name alone.

records.title: IPEDS occupational category
records.excerpt: The primary occupational activity classification used to aggregate employees in the IPEDS HR component.
records.body: Each reportable employee is assigned to the applicable current IPEDS/SOC-aligned occupational category based on primary duties. Job title alone may not be sufficient to determine the correct category.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Human Resources and SOC resources
records.use: Use the governed HR crosswalk and current SOC guidance; retain unresolved mappings for review.

records.title: Tenure status
records.excerpt: The governed HR classification of a reportable instructional employee as tenured, on tenure track, or not on tenure track.
records.body: Tenure status is separate from academic rank, full-time status, and faculty title. It must come from the institutional HR appointment record and be mapped to the current IPEDS reporting categories.
records.use: Use only for employees in the applicable HR reporting population.

records.title: Faculty headcount
records.excerpt: A distinct-person count of employees included in the governed faculty population.
records.body: Faculty headcount counts people once within the selected reporting population. The institutional faculty population and the narrower IPEDS instructional-staff population may differ, so the selected definition must be shown with the result.
records.source: EduInsight HR source contract and NCES IPEDS HR
records.use: State whether the result is all institutional faculty or the IPEDS instructional-staff population.

records.title: Faculty full-time equivalent (FTE)
records.excerpt: A workload-equivalent measure of faculty staffing, distinct from the count of individual employees.
records.body: Faculty FTE converts full- and part-time appointments into a comparable workload measure under a governed institutional methodology. It is not necessarily the same as IPEDS student FTE or a faculty headcount.
records.use: The appointment-to-FTE conversion policy must be supplied and approved before this metric is certified.

records.title: Student-to-faculty ratio
records.excerpt: The IPEDS ratio of student FTE to instructional-staff FTE after applying the component's inclusion and exclusion rules.
records.body: The ratio is not total student headcount divided by all employees. Its student and instructional-staff populations follow the applicable Fall Enrollment instructions, including exclusions for certain students and staff.
records.calculation: applicable student FTE / applicable instructional-staff FTE
records.use: Use the current EF specification and show both contributing populations.

records.title: Institutional control
records.excerpt: The IPEDS classification of an institution as public, private nonprofit, or private for-profit.
records.body: Institutional control is a core Institutional Characteristics field that affects applicable survey forms and comparisons. The current institution profile is governed as public.
records.use: Verify annually because the IC header controls downstream component applicability.

records.title: Institution level
records.excerpt: The IPEDS classification based on the highest award level offered by the institution.
records.body: Institution level distinguishes four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions under IPEDS rules. The current profile is governed as a four-year degree-granting institution.
records.use: Do not infer level from the institution name; use the governed award offerings and current IC instructions.

records.title: Calendar system
records.excerpt: The method by which the institution structures most courses for the academic year.
records.body: Common IPEDS calendar systems include semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, program-based, and continuous enrollment. The current institution profile is governed as semester-based, and that selection affects Cost, Fall Enrollment, Graduation Rates, and Student Financial Aid reporting.
records.use: Verify in the IC header before preparing other components.

records.title: Credit hour
records.excerpt: A unit used to measure academic work under the institution's approved credit-hour policy and applicable federal requirements.
records.body: Credit hours represent an amount of student work defined through the institution's academic and regulatory policy. They support enrollment-load, instructional-activity, and program-length calculations; they are not interchangeable with clock hours.
records.use: Use the approved institutional policy and program modality. Do not derive credits solely from scheduled contact time without the authorized conversion.

records.title: Clock hour
records.excerpt: A measured period of instructional time used by applicable programs and federal reporting rules.
records.body: A clock hour measures scheduled instructional activity and is distinct from a credit hour. Programs reported in clock hours must follow the applicable institutional and federal definitions and any approved credit-hour conversion rules.
records.use: Use only for programs whose governed unit of instructional activity is clock hours.

records.title: Academic term
records.excerpt: A defined instructional period, such as a semester or quarter, with governed start, end, and census dates.
records.body: A term is an institutional instructional period. It is different from an IPEDS collection period: Fall, Winter, and Spring collections describe federal reporting windows, not necessarily the term in which the underlying activity occurred.
records.use: State the term and year when a point-in-time or term-specific metric is requested.

records.title: Academic year
records.excerpt: The institution's governed instructional year, usually spanning parts of two calendar years.
records.body: For a traditional calendar, an academic year generally covers two semesters or trimesters, three quarters, or a 4-1-4 period. It differs from a calendar year, aid year, collection year, and the July-through-June 12-month enrollment period unless a specification explicitly aligns them.
records.source: NCES IPEDS glossary and institutional calendar
records.use: Always display both years, such as 2025-26, when the period spans two calendar years.

records.title: Class standing
records.excerpt: An institutional student level, such as first-year, sophomore, junior, or senior, assigned under the academic policy.
records.body: Class standing usually depends on earned credits or institutional progression rules. It is not the same as first-time status, cohort year, or undergraduate/graduate level.
records.use: The current upload does not include an approved class-standing derivation. Supply the registrar policy before computing this dimension.

records.title: Degree/certificate-seeking student
records.excerpt: A student recognized by the institution as seeking a degree, certificate, or other recognized postsecondary credential.
records.body: Degree/certificate-seeking status is an institutional classification used throughout IPEDS cohorts and enrollment categories. Enrollment in credit-bearing coursework alone does not necessarily establish this status.
records.use: Resolve from the governed student program/intent record; do not infer from course level.

records.title: Non-degree/certificate-seeking student
records.excerpt: A student taking reportable coursework who is not recognized as seeking a degree, certificate, or other formal credential.
records.body: Non-degree/certificate-seeking is not a synonym for part-time or continuing education. The student may take credit-bearing courses while remaining outside a credential-seeking program.
records.use: Use the governed program-intent status and the component's inclusion rules.

records.title: Credential or award level
records.excerpt: The level of a recognized postsecondary credential, such as certificate, associate's, bachelor's, master's, or doctorate.
records.body: Credential level describes the award itself. It differs from student class standing and from the institution's IPEDS level. For Completions import files, the credential maps to an allowed AWLEVEL code.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Completions and Institutional Characteristics
records.use: Use the governed credential catalog and current AWLEVEL crosswalk.

records.title: Academic program
records.excerpt: A governed curriculum leading toward a defined educational objective or recognized credential.
records.body: An academic program is the institutionally approved curriculum entity used for enrollment, completions, and program reporting. A program may have one or more majors or concentrations, but those terms should not be treated as interchangeable unless the catalog mapping says they are.
records.use: Resolve program names and codes through the governed catalog before filtering students or completions.

records.title: Major
records.excerpt: A student's formally declared primary or secondary field of study within the institutional curriculum.
records.body: A major is a student-program relationship and may differ from the broader academic program entity or its CIP reporting code. Multiple majors require explicit ordering and effective dates.
records.source: Governed academic catalog and student-program records
records.use: State whether primary majors, second majors, or both are included.

records.title: Concentration
records.excerpt: An approved area of emphasis nested within an academic program or major.
records.body: A concentration is narrower than a program or major and may not map to a separate IPEDS CIP code. It should be reported only when the governed catalog and source record identify it explicitly.
records.use: Do not infer a concentration from course-taking behavior.

records.title: Full-time and part-time attendance status
records.excerpt: A term-level enrollment-load classification determined under the applicable institutional and reporting rules.
records.body: The current undergraduate source contract treats fewer than 12 semester credits as inconsistent with full-time status. Federal rules set 12 semester or quarter hours as the undergraduate minimum for many term-based programs, while graduate full-time workload is institution-defined.
records.source: Institutional enrollment-status contract and Federal Student Aid Handbook
records.use: Undergraduate 12-credit validation is available. A governed graduate full-time policy has not been supplied and must not be invented.

records.title: Duplicated headcount
records.excerpt: A count in which the same student can appear more than once across terms, programs, or reporting units.
records.body: Duplicated headcount counts qualifying records or appearances rather than unique people over the whole selected period. It may be useful for activity analysis but must never be labeled unduplicated enrollment.
records.use: Disclose the duplication grain, such as student-term or student-program.

records.title: Unduplicated headcount
records.excerpt: A distinct-person count in which each student is counted once across the defined reporting period.
records.body: IPEDS 12-month enrollment uses an unduplicated headcount across its reporting period. Unduplicated does not mean the same thing as Fall census headcount because the reporting windows and included activity differ.
records.calculation: COUNT(DISTINCT reportable student_id) across the defined period
records.use: Use for the July-through-June E12 population; use Fall headcount for the certified point-in-time census.

records.title: New student
records.excerpt: An institutional label for a student newly entering the reporting institution in a defined period.
records.body: New student is broader than first-time student unless the institution explicitly defines the two populations as identical. A new student may be first-time, transfer-in, or another non-first-time entrant, depending on the governed reporting context.
records.use: Always state which entry categories are included. Do not substitute new student for the narrower IPEDS first-time population.

records.title: Continuing or returning student
records.excerpt: A degree/certificate-seeking student who is neither first-time nor transfer-in for the applicable reporting classification.
records.body: Continuing/returning is an enrollment-status category, not proof of continuous enrollment. A student returning after a stop-out may be included when the component and institutional status rules place the student in this category.
records.use: Use the governed entry-status field; do not infer solely from class standing.

records.title: Transfer-in student
records.excerpt: A student entering the reporting institution with prior postsecondary attendance after high school under the applicable reporting rules.
records.body: Transfer-in describes entry into this institution and is distinct from transfer-out. Credits earned before high school completion do not by themselves make an undergraduate a transfer-in student under the first-time definition.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Fall Enrollment and Outcome Measures
records.use: Resolve from governed prior-attendance and transfer-entry records.

records.title: Transfer-out student
records.excerpt: A student known to have subsequently enrolled at another postsecondary institution under the applicable outcome definition.
records.body: Transfer-out is an outcome after attendance at the reporting institution. Reliable identification generally requires an external enrollment source such as National Student Clearinghouse data; absence from the local SIS does not prove transfer.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Graduation Rates and external enrollment records
records.use: The current local warehouse cannot establish transfers to other institutions without an external subsequent-enrollment source.

records.title: Stop-out
records.excerpt: A temporary break in enrollment followed by a return within the governed observation window.
records.body: Stop-out is an observed enrollment pattern, not a permanent outcome. The permitted gap and observation window must be defined before the measure is calculated.
records.use: The current catalog does not assert a universal gap length. Approve the institutional definition before reporting a stop-out rate.

records.title: Dropout
records.excerpt: A student outcome that requires an explicit observation window and evidence that distinguishes departure from stop-out, transfer, completion, or continuing enrollment.
records.body: A missing local enrollment record does not by itself establish that a student dropped out. The institution must define the observation window and account for completion and external enrollment before applying this label.
records.use: Do not calculate from the local SIS alone when subsequent enrollment elsewhere is unknown.

records.title: Persistence
records.excerpt: Continued enrollment or completion across a defined period, potentially at the same institution or at another institution.
records.body: Persistence must state whether it means continued activity at this institution only or at any institution. Institution-only persistence can use local records; any-institution persistence requires an external subsequent-enrollment source. Persistence is broader than the governed IPEDS first-year retention rate.
records.use: Local persistence is computable when the cohort and window are specified. Any-institution persistence is not supported without Clearinghouse or equivalent data.

records.title: Tuition discount rate
records.excerpt: Institution-funded grant aid divided by gross tuition and fee revenue for a defined population and period.
records.body: Tuition discount rate is a finance and enrollment-management measure, not an IPEDS net-price calculation. Institutions may use different scopes, such as first-time undergraduates or all undergraduates, so the population and aid source must be stated.
records.calculation: institution-funded grant aid / gross tuition and required fee revenue
records.numerator: Institution-funded grant aid for the defined population
records.denominator: Gross tuition and required fee revenue for the same population and period
records.use: The current warehouse lacks an approved gross-tuition and institutional-aid contract for this metric.

records.title: Instructional activity
records.excerpt: Reportable credit-hour and clock-hour activity used by the IPEDS 12-month Enrollment component to derive student FTE.
records.body: Instructional activity is the annual volume of reportable credit hours and, where applicable, clock hours generated during the 12-month reporting period. Undergraduate and graduate credit-hour activity are reported separately, and the applicable IPEDS rules determine which activity belongs in the FTE calculation.
records.calculation: SUM(reportable attempted credit hours or clock hours) for the applicable level and reporting period
records.denominator: Not applicable until activity is converted to FTE
records.use: Use the same annual period, student levels, calendar basis, and exclusions required by the current E12 specification.

records.title: Distance education enrollment status
records.excerpt: The governed classification of a student as enrolled exclusively, enrolled in some, or not enrolled in distance education courses.
records.body: IPEDS distance-education status is based on the student's reportable course enrollment during the applicable survey period. Exclusively distance education, some but not all distance education, and no distance education are mutually exclusive categories and must reconcile to the applicable enrollment population.
records.source: NCES IPEDS 12-month Enrollment and Fall Enrollment distance-education instructions
records.use: Classify from governed course-modality records; do not infer distance status from a student's program or campus alone.

records.title: Dual enrollment
records.excerpt: High school students enrolled in college courses for credit, either within or outside a formal dual-enrollment program.
records.body: For IPEDS 12-month Enrollment reporting, institutions identify whether high school students took college courses for credit and report the applicable unduplicated population. Participation in a formal dual-enrollment program is distinguished from high school enrollment outside such a program.
records.source: NCES IPEDS 12-month Enrollment (E12), Parts E and F
records.use: Use governed high-school and college-credit indicators; do not infer dual enrollment solely from age.

records.title: U.S. nonresident reporting category
records.excerpt: The current IPEDS reporting category for a person who is not a citizen or national of the United States and is in the country on an applicable temporary visa.
records.body: U.S. nonresident is a federal reporting category and is not interchangeable with institutional residency for tuition purposes, international recruitment status, or place of residence. The current IPEDS specification and citizenship/visa source control the classification.
records.use: Do not derive this category from the domestic/international display label alone; retain the governed citizenship and visa mapping.

records.title: Race/ethnicity reporting category
records.excerpt: The mutually exclusive federal reporting classification used in applicable IPEDS enrollment, completions, and outcomes tables.
records.body: IPEDS race/ethnicity categories are derived through the federal reporting sequence and include a separate U.S. nonresident category and an unknown category where applicable. They are reporting classifications, not a substitute for the more detailed identities a student may provide.
records.use: Apply the current federal mapping consistently and preserve unknown values rather than assigning an unsupported category.

records.title: Sex reporting category
records.excerpt: The sex classification accepted by the applicable IPEDS collection-year specification, including unknown when the current form permits it.
records.body: The reporting categories and accepted codes are controlled by the current IPEDS survey specification. Institutional gender-identity data must not be silently remapped into a federal sex category without an approved crosswalk.
records.use: Use the collection-year code set and retain unknown values where supported; do not reuse a prior-year code that the current form removed.

records.title: Instructional-staff full-time equivalent (FTE)
records.excerpt: The workload-equivalent instructional-staff measure used in the IPEDS student-to-faculty ratio.
records.body: Instructional-staff FTE applies the current IPEDS inclusion, exclusion, and part-time conversion rules to the reportable instructional-staff population. It is narrower than all-employee FTE and may differ from an institution's internal faculty-workload FTE.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Fall Enrollment and institutional HR workload policy
records.use: Do not certify the value until the employee population and appointment-to-FTE conversion are governed for the applicable reporting year.

records.title: Normal time to completion
records.excerpt: The amount of time a student would normally take to complete a program according to the institution's published program length.
records.body: Normal time is program-specific and provides the reference period for IPEDS graduation-rate windows such as 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time. It is not the observed average time students actually take to graduate.
records.source: NCES IPEDS Graduation Rates instructions and institutional program catalog
records.use: Resolve from the governed program length and credential; do not apply one institution-wide duration to every program.

records.title: Accreditation
records.excerpt: Public recognition granted by an accrediting agency after evaluating an institution or program against its standards.
records.body: Institutional accreditation generally applies to the institution as a whole; specialized or programmatic accreditation applies to a program, department, or school. The U.S. Department of Education recognizes accrediting agencies that meet federal criteria, but the Department does not directly accredit institutions.
records.source: U.S. Department of Education accreditation guidance
records.use: Identify the accrediting agency, accredited scope, status, and effective period; do not infer accreditation from program approval alone.

records.title: Title IV federal student aid
records.excerpt: Federal student-aid programs authorized under Title IV of the Higher Education Act.
records.body: Title IV includes federal grants, work-study, and loan programs administered under the Higher Education Act. IPEDS participation and several reported cohorts use Title IV status, but Title IV recipient, Pell recipient, and aid applicant are not interchangeable populations.
records.source: U.S. Department of Education Federal Student Aid and NCES IPEDS
records.use: Use the governed aid-award source and the exact cohort required by the current reporting specification.

records.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
records.excerpt: The federal law protecting the privacy of student education records and granting eligible students rights over those records.
records.body: FERPA applies to education records maintained by covered educational agencies and institutions. At the postsecondary level, rights transfer to the eligible student. Personally identifiable information includes direct and indirect identifiers that can identify a student alone or in combination.
records.source: U.S. Department of Education Student Privacy Policy Office
records.use: EduInsight's aggregate-first privacy boundary remains stricter than merely removing names; identifiable row-level requests must be refused or routed through an authorized governed workflow.
